raw_text:
Great. Below is a structured 12-week muscle-gain program for a 26-year-old female client who is a strict vegan, recreational lifter, with access to a full gym. The plan emphasizes progressive overload, balanced hypertrophy across major muscle groups, adequate recovery, and a nutrition strategy to hit ~150 g protein/day from plant sources. Adjust weights and volumes to match her current strength and progression.

Assumptions and goals
- Training frequency: 4 days/week resistance training + optional 1–2 cardio/pelvic stability days if desired.
- Weekly protein target: ~150 g. Calorie target: slight surplus to support muscle gain (roughly +250–500 kcal/day above maintenance; adjust after 2–4 weeks based on progress).
- Rest between sets: 60–90 seconds for hypertrophy, 2–3 minutes for compounds or heavier sets.
- Progression: progressive overload each week by increasing load, reps, or sets within safe limits.
- Vegan protein sources are emphasized (see nutrition section).

Phase structure (12 weeks)
- Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Hypertrophy foundation, 4-day split)
- Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Intensification and progressive overload, 4-day split while introducing advanced techniques)
- Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Peaking for higher strength and muscle gain, 4-day split with refinements)

Weekly schedule (example)
- Day 1: Upper Body Push (chest, shoulders, triceps)
- Day 2: Lower Body (quad-dominant)
- Day 3: Rest or light cardio/low-impact conditioning
- Day 4: Upper Body Pull (back, biceps, rear delts)
- Day 5: Lower Body (posterior chain, glutes)
- Day 6: Optional active recovery or cardio
- Day 7: Rest

Phase 1 details (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: establish technique, build baseline hypertrophy, reinforce nutrition habits.

Weeks 1–4: 4-day split
- Week 1 and 2: 3–4 sets per exercise, 8–12 reps per set
- Week 3 and 4: 4–5 sets per exercise, 8–12 reps (slightly higher volume)

Day A – Upper Push
- Barbell bench press or floor press: 4 x 8–12
- Dumbbell incline press: 3 x 8–12
- Overhead press (dumbbell or barbell): 3 x 8–12
- Dumbbell lateral raises: 3 x 12–15
- Cable triceps pushdown or overhead triceps extension (vegan-friendly): 3 x 10–12
- Push-ups or ring push-ups (optional): 2 x 8–12

Day B – Lower Body (Quad-dominant)
- Back squat or front squat: 4 x 8–12
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8–12 per leg
- Leg press (if available): 3 x 10–12
- Leg extensions: 3 x 12–15
- Calf raises: 4 x 12–20
- Core work (plank variations): 3 x 30–60 seconds

Day C – Upper Pull
- Pull-ups or lat pulldown: 4 x 8–12
- Barbell or dumbbell rows: 3 x 8–12
- Seated cable row or t-bar row: 3 x 8–12
- Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Dumbbell biceps curl (hammer or standard): 3 x 10–12
- Rear delt flyes: 3 x 12–15

Day D – Lower Body (Posterior chain)
- Deadlift variants (conventional, sumo, or Romanian): 3–4 x 6–10
- Hip thrust or glute bridge: 3–4 x 8–12
- Dumbbell hip hinge or good mornings: 3 x 10–12
- Hamstring curls (machine or stability ball): 3 x 12–15
- Calf raises: 3 x 12–20
- Core: 3 x 12–15 Russian twists or hanging leg raises

Progression notes for Phase 1
- Aim to add 2.5–5 kg on compound lifts every 2 weeks if technique is solid and reps are achievable.
- If form deteriorates, stay at the current load and focus on technique.
- Ensure at least 48 hours between sessions targeting similar muscle groups.

Phase 2 details (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase training density, introduce progressive overload with form of advanced techniques, maintain hypertrophy.

Week structure: 4-day split, similar layout with adjustments
- Increase sets on compounds to 4–5 sets per exercise where tolerable
- Reps in 6–10 for main lifts to build strength and mass
- Introduce tempo work and occasional supersets for accessory movements

Day A – Upper Push (increased intensity)
- Barbell bench press: 4–5 x 6–10
- Dumbbell incline press: 3–4 x 8–12
- Overhead press: 3–4 x 6–10
- Lateral raises: 3–4 x 12–15
- Dips or close-grip bench (machine-assisted if needed): 3 x 8–12
- Triceps extension: 3 x 10–12

Day B – Lower Body Quad Focus
- Back squat or front squat: 4–5 x 6–10
- Bulgarian split squat: 3–4 x 8–12
- Leg press: 3–4 x 8–12
- Leg extensions: 3 x 12–15
- Calf raises: 4 x 12–20
- Core: 3 x 12–15

Day C – Upper Pull
- Weighted pull-ups or lat pulldown: 4–5 x 6–10
- Barbell row: 3–4 x 6–10
- Seated row: 3–4 x 8–12
- Face pulls: 3–4 x 12–15
- Dumbbell curls: 3 x 10–12
- Rear delt flyes: 3 x 12–15

Day D – Lower Body Romain/Posterior
- Deadlift variant or Romanian deadlift: 4 x 6–10
- Hip thrust or glute bridge: 3–4 x 8–12
- Hamstring curls: 3 x 12–15
- Glute-focused accessory (reverse lunges, step-ups): 3 x 8–12 per leg
- Calf raises: 4 x 12–20
- Core: 3 x 12–15

Advanced techniques (optional, rotate every 1–2 weeks)
- Drop sets: after final set of a chosen exercise (e.g., leg extensions or lateral raises)
- Tempo variations: e.g., 3–0–1–0 for squats or bench
- Post-activation potentiation: light set before heavy main set on one exercise per day

Phase 3 details (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: maximal hypertrophy and sustainable gains; refine technique and optimize nutrition.

Weeks 9–12: 4-day split with periodized loading
- Main lifts: 4–5 x 5–8 reps on heavy days
- Accessory work: 3–4 x 8–12 reps
- Include one lighter deload-style week if needed or keep training heavy but reduce total volume slightly in Week 12 to facilitate recovery before any potential future cycles.

Day A – Upper Push (Power + Hypertrophy)
- Barbell bench press: 4–5 x 5–8
- Overhead press: 3–4 x 5–8
- Incline dumbbell press: 3–4 x 8–12
- Lateral raises: 3–4 x 12–15
- Triceps pushdown: 3–4 x 8–12

Day B – Lower Body Quad/Glute Focus
- Back squat or front squat: 4–5 x 5–8
- Bulgarian split squat: 3–4 x 6–10 per leg
- Leg press: 3–4 x 8–12
- Romanian deadlift: 3–4 x 6–10
- Calf raises: 4 x 12–20
- Core: 3 x 12–15

Day C – Upper Pull
- Weighted pull-ups or lat pulldown: 4–5 x 5–8
- Barbell or dumbbell row: 3–4 x 6–10
- Seated row: 3–4 x 8–12
- Face pulls: 3–4 x 12–15
- Dumbbell curls or preacher curls: 3 x 8–12

Day D – Lower Body Posterior
- Deadlift variation: 3–4 x 4–6 or 5–8 if using sumo/deficit
- Hip thrust: 4 x 6–10
- Hamstring curls: 3–4 x 8–12
- Glute activation/accessory: glute bridges or band walks: 3 x 12–20
- Calf raises: 4 x 12–20
- Core: 3 x 12–15

Nutrition plan to hit 150 g protein/day (plant-based)
Overall aim: ~2.0–2.4 g/kg protein daily if body weight is around 65–75 kg (adjust target based on actual body weight and progress). For a 26-year-old recreational lifter, a practical target is about 1.8–2.2 g/kg protein daily. If weight is 65 kg, target ~117–143 g. To hit 150 g, plan would be around 2.3 g/kg if weight ≈65 kg; adjust to match actual weight. The client asked specifically for 150 g from plant sources, so plan to distribute protein evenly across meals and include protein-rich vegan foods.

Estimated daily protein distribution (example for ~150 g)
- Breakfast: 30–35 g
  - Options: plant-based Greek-style yogurt (soy-based) + 1–2 scoops of vegan protein powder (pea/rice blend), or tofu scramble with soy yogurt on the side, plus quinoa or tempeh.
- Snack: 20–25 g
  - Options: protein shake with pea/rice blend + a handful of almonds or a protein bar made from soy/pea protein.
- Lunch: 30 g
  - Options: lentil or chickpea-based dish with quinoa, edamame, hemp seeds on top.
- Snack: 20–25 g
  - Options: hummus and whole-grain pita with chickpeas, or a smoothie with vegan protein powder, flaxseed, and soy milk.
- Dinner: 30–35 g
  - Options: tempeh or seitan-based main + beans or lentils as a side; quinoa or brown rice; vegetables.

Plant protein sources high in protein per serving
- Tempeh: ~15–21 g per 3–4 oz
- Tofu: ~8–15 g per 3 oz (firm tofu higher)
- Seitan: ~25 g per 3 oz (gluten-based; not suitable for those with gluten sensitivity)
- Lentils: ~18 g per cooked cup
- Chickpeas: ~15 g per cooked cup
- Black beans: ~15 g per cooked cup
- Edamame: ~17 g per cooked cup
- Quinoa: ~8 g per cooked cup
- Hemp seeds: ~10 g per 3 tbsp
- Chia seeds: ~5 g per 2 tbsp
- Nutritional yeast: ~8 g per 2 tbsp
- Pea protein powder: ~20–25 g per scoop
- Rice protein powder: ~20 g per scoop (often lower digestibility when used alone; combine with pea for better amino profile)

Daily protein plan example (two shakes + meals)
- Breakfast: tofu/tempeh scramble + 1 scoop vegan protein in smoothie: 35 g
- Snack: protein shake with 1 scoop pea/rice + 1–2 tbsp peanut butter: 25 g
- Lunch: lentil quinoa bowl with edamame: 30 g
- Snack: chickpeas and pita + 2 tbsp hummus: 20 g
- Dinner: tempeh or seitan-based main + beans: 40 g
- Total: ~150 g

Other nutrition considerations
- Caloric target: start with maintenance + 250–500 kcal/day for muscle gain. Track weight weekly and adjust by ±250 kcal if weight gain is too slow (<0.25–0.5 kg per week) or too fast (>0.75 kg per week, which risks fat gain).
- Carbohydrates: adequate to fuel workouts; focus on whole grains, fruits, vegetables, legumes, and starches (potatoes, sweet potatoes, oats, rice, etc.).
- Fats: include healthy fats for hormonal balance (avocados, nuts, seeds, olive oil, flaxseed).
- Vitamin B12: essential for vegans; supplement 250–500 mcg daily or as per labeling.
- Vitamin D: estimate daily intake; consider supplement if deficient or insufficient sun exposure.
- Iron: plant-based iron is non-heme; pair with vitamin C sources to improve absorption; consider iron status checks; include foods like lentils, chickpeas, spinach, fortified cereals.
- Zinc: include in diet via beans, nuts, seeds, whole grains; consider supplementation if requirements not met.
- Calcium: ensure intake from fortified plant milks, tofu made with calcium sulfate, leafy greens (kale, bok choy), fortified cereals.
- Omega-3: include alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) rich sources (chia seeds, flaxseeds, walnuts). Consider algae-based DHA/EPA supplement if needed.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly.
- Hydration: 2–3 liters water/day, adjust for activity level.
- Mobility and warmups: include 5–10 minutes of dynamic warm-up and 5–10 minutes of mobility work daily.
- Deload: if fatigue accumulates, implement a light deload week (lower volume by ~50%) in week 7 or 11, depending on recovery markers.

Notes on injuries and form
- Prioritize technique especially on compound lifts (squat, deadlift, bench).
- Use proper evidence-based form cues and adjust volumes if any joint pain arises.
- Replace any exercise not suitable with a safe alternative (e.g., swap barbell back squat for goblet squat if needed).

Progress tracking
- Record weekly weights and reps; track body measurements (arms, chest, waist, hips, thighs).
- Take progress photos every 4 weeks.
- Adjust nutrition and training based on progress every 2–4 weeks.

Safety and variability
- If the client has any medical concerns or dietary restrictions beyond veganism, consult with a physician or dietitian.
